title: AI game rush - AI game bust
author: purri-cat-studio
selftext:
Browsing steam next fest and it’s true. There’s an insane amount of games. 

I’m not bothered nor worried. 

The shovel was invented, perfected, and now there’s a gold rush with many thinking their version of a tower defence or vampire survivors clone will make them rich. 

Once the majority get lose their $100 I expect the gold rush to be over and the few successful folks to continue making quality games, with AI tools. 

I do think Steam should raise their registration fee though.

comments.author: Head-Job8397
comments.body:
Sorry if the translation sounds weird.

I’ve given up on AI game development. I thought, “Since I was able to create a decent open-world 3D map with three.js using AI, maybe I can pull off game development?” So I installed Unity and Blender, but it got really tough from there, and it was just too much for me. Even with AI, it takes a lot of perseverance to see a game project through to the end. Of course, it depends on the quality, and future AI might make it easier, but at least right now, AI game development is surprisingly tough. It’s easy to develop simple web apps with AI, but as soon as you get into games, it suddenly gets a lot harder. Good luck with your game development.

replies.author: Usual-Response-1312
replies.body: capitalism is the issue because it's creating the wrong incentive structure where we exploit needs to create maximum profit instead of creating for our needs directly

replies.author: Time_Cat_5212
replies.body:
Yes, our economic system optimizes for the allocation of privileges within the population, not the overall benefit of human civilization.

That's why things like the paperclip dilemma are so relevant.  You'll have an AI system optimized to maximize production of some product, or whatever, say it's attention to ads or something instead of paperclips... And that causes harm, or at least falls way short of AI's potential to benefit the world.

comments.author: ThreeDMK
comments.body:
This has been going on since last year.  It is never publicized, but I know of at least two big name AAA studios that signed big contracts with Devin UI and others to help facilitate shifts to agentic development.  They are doing it because others are doing it.

At the same time though, many of these same studios have significant infighting going on.  There are large groups of people who are so anti-ai that adoption has been difficult.

Source:  I previously worked for Bethesda, have many friends in the industry spanning 15+ years.  Shit is wild right now for game devs.  :( I am glad I got out when I did.

comments.author: heskey30
comments.body: Gross. I can't believe how many devs want our monopolist overlords to charge developers more arbitrary fees. Suddenly capital as a barrier to entry is good? Is ths astroturfing?

replies.author: Almaravarion
replies.body: Are the monopolists in the room with us right now? Capital to entry is not 'good', it is 'necessary evil'. Intent here would be to discourage low level slop that has no chance of making listing price back, from effectively flooding the marketplaces. Alternatively a vetting process to reduce or void that would be fine, though unfortunately it would require quite extensive input in manpower, and would instead introduce risk of human manipulation.

replies.author: heskey30
replies.body: Steam gets a massive cut from almost every game sold on PC. If their store sucks it's not because they don't have enough resources to curate it properly. It's because they don't need to, because there's nowhere else for players to go. They don't need to take EVEN MORE from developers. They need people to stop putting them on a pedestal so they'll get off their ass and improve their product after 20 years of stagnation.

replies.author: Almaravarion
replies.body:
Which is exactly why other stores by major companies took almost all of their customers, despite steam giving away tons of games for free...

Oh, wait, sorry, that was Epic Games' Launcher instead; my bad.

Steam is not perfect; Far from it, but frankly it is one of the best game stores on the planet currently. Alongside GOG, which itself, while having some better elements, is lacking few features present on Steam.

comments.author: Time_Cat_5212
comments.body:
Yeah there's plenty of stupidity on both ends.

The luddite's fallacy is basically overlooking the good uses of new tech because of the bad uses.  Makes it harder to be critical without sounding backward.

The hypesters are obnoxious, too. Their uncritical obsession with automating every aspect of human life and work is unrealistic and reckless, and it only energizes the luddites.

comments.author: Big_Membership9737
comments.body: For most people, in the current economy, it's more like buying a lottery ticket; they would buy it for anything. The problem isn't the number of games or the AI. The issue is that everything is half-backed and lacks effort. All of these fundamentals are missing. If the game is good, players will want to play it, and it will meet their expectations. Then, you can sell it everywhere. You don't need Steam. You can also make your own website, etc.
